description: Count unrestricted and Brauer shortest addition chains for a bounded target.

source.title: Rosetta Code: Addition chains
source.algorithm_reference: OEIS A003313 and the standard addition-chain definition
source.source_license: Rosetta Code content is GNU Free Documentation License 1.2 according to its copyright page; algorithm idea only, with no prose, code, examples, fixtures, or tests reused

output.encoding: [minimum_length, brauer_chain_count, non_brauer_chain_count] as signed 64-bit little-endian words

workspace.meaning: Fixed target-indexed candidate mask, one chain workspace, recursion state, and three staged output words

contract.operation: Return the minimum unrestricted addition-chain length and the counts of shortest Brauer and non-Brauer chains.
contract.chain_rule: Start with 1; each strictly larger term is the sum of two earlier terms, which may be equal.
contract.brauer_rule: Every new term in a Brauer chain is the previous term plus any earlier term.
contract.search: Iteratively deepen from ceil(log2(target)) through the binary-chain upper bound; enumerate each distinct next sum once.
contract.pruning: Reject a prefix if doubling its last term for every remaining step still cannot reach the target.
contract.complexity: Exponential in minimum chain length, with O(L^2) candidate-addend pairs per prefix for chain length L; fixed target bound 31.
contract.tie_rule: Chain counts ignore the order in which addend pairs produce the same next term.
contract.error_precedence: Validate and compute the result before checking output pointer and capacity.
